title: Meet the king
objectives: Understand the king moves one square in any direction
Understand the king can never move to a square an enemy piece attacks

steps.text: The king moves just one square in any direction — straight or diagonal. He's the piece you must always protect, which comes with a strict rule: the king can never move to a square an enemy piece attacks, even if nothing is there yet.

steps.prompt: Move the king exactly one square in any direction.

hints.text: Move the king exactly one square, any direction.
Any of the eight neighboring squares works.
The king steps from e4 to e5.

feedback.default: The king can only move one square at a time — not further.

steps.successExplanation: That's a legal king move — one square, onto a square nothing attacks.

steps.prompt: Capture the undefended black pawn with your king.

hints.text: The king captures the same way it moves — one square, in any direction.
The pawn is one square diagonally from your king.
The king captures on d5 — one diagonal step.

feedback.default: The king can capture like any other piece — move exactly one square onto the enemy piece. But only if nothing else attacks that square.

steps.successExplanation: Kxd5 captures the pawn. The king can capture a piece one square away, as long as no other enemy piece defends that square — capturing into an attacked square is never legal.

steps.prompt: The king can move to a square right next to the enemy king.

feedback.default: Two kings can never stand next to each other — that square would always be attacked by the enemy king, which the king-can't-move-into-check rule forbids.

steps.successExplanation: Right — it's the same rule as any attacked square: the king can never move somewhere an enemy piece (including the other king) attacks.
